comparison.objective: Laminate task removes three spacer dowels so a registered sheet settles and bonds to a drawer front; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber for repeatable non-bottoming stops.
comparison.physical_skill: Laminate task tests sequential long-dowel extraction while avoiding sheet drag, tilt, slide, or premature misbonding. Candidate tests recessed-key insertion, counterholding, unlocking, fine collar rotation, bounded tightening, and feedback-driven repeated cycling.
comparison.success_condition: Laminate: each of three compliant panels bonds within 1 mm and 3° while remaining within 6 mm x/8 mm y registration; all panels count for 1 s with tools ≥3 cm away. Candidate requires two valid physical impacts, prescribed energy/velocity/stroke limits, retention, and enumerated safety failures. No separate task spec version is available for PR-1130; its body does not state explicit dowel-loss/damage-force limits, while candidate lacks numeric rebound, overload, lock-torque, and drift thresholds.
comparison.reason: Managing irreversible settling during support extraction is materially different from tool-mediated parameter adjustment and evaluation of dynamic stopping response. Their shared need to avoid disturbing a supported object is only generic.
